children: Indian shares were off to a muted start on Wednesday as persistent foreign fund outflows offset positive cues from Asian markets, while concerns over the Middle East conflict remained an overhang.

Eleven of the 16 major sectors logged gains. The broader small-caps

Asian shares were headed for a sixth consecutive session of gains on Wednesday, as signs of continued consumer demand for AI-related applications supported technology stocks. MSCI's broadest index for Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MISX00000PUS) rose 0.7%.

Foreign investors continued to shun Indian equities, with provisional data showing net sales of 38.1 billion rupees ($398.58 million) on Tuesday, marking their eighth selling session in the last nine trading days.
Overseas traders have sold Indian shares worth $1.81 billion so far in September, taking year-to-date outflows to $25.87 billion.
